# Sirach Chapter 13 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 13 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_013_page_001.jpg

---

**13:1** Handle pitch and you'll get dirty; hang around an arrogant person and you'll become just like them.

**13:2** Don't take on more than you can carry, and don't get mixed up with people who are far above you in wealth and power. What does a clay pot have in common with an iron kettle? The iron strikes and the clay shatters.

**13:3** When a rich man does wrong, he adds insults to it; when a poor man is wronged, he has to apologize.

**13:4** If you're useful to them, they'll use you; when you're not, they'll drop you.

**13:5** As long as you have something, they'll stay close — they'll drain you dry and feel nothing.

**13:6** Do they need something from you? Watch out — they'll flatter you, smile at you, get your hopes up. They'll say all the right things: "What can I do for you?"

**13:7** Then they'll humiliate you at their table — not just once, but again and again — until you have nothing left. And in the end, they'll laugh at you. After that, when they happen to see you on the street, they'll walk right past with a shake of the head.

**13:8** Be careful — don't get taken in, and don't make yourself look foolish chasing their invitations.

**13:9** When a powerful person invites you somewhere, learn to hold back — and they'll only want you more.

**13:10** Don't crowd in too close or you'll be pushed out; don't hang too far back or you'll be overlooked.

**13:11** Don't try to talk to them as an equal, and don't believe everything they say — all that talk is a test, and their smile is an examination.

**13:12** Someone who doesn't know mercy is someone who doesn't know when to stop talking — and they'll give you nothing but grief.

**13:13** Be very, very careful — you're on the edge of your own ruin. When you hear these warnings, take them to heart even in your sleep.

**13:14** Love the Lord throughout your whole life, and call on him when you need to be saved.

**13:15** Every creature is drawn to its own kind, and people naturally gravitate toward those like themselves.

**13:16** All living things stay with their own; people are no different — we seek our own kind.

**13:17** What does a wolf have to do with a lamb? A sinner has no more business with the righteous.

**13:18** Can a hyena and a dog ever get along? Can a rich person and a poor person?

**13:19** In the wilderness, lions feed on wild donkeys — just as the rich feed on the poor.

**13:20** Pride finds poverty revolting; the rich feel the same about the poor.

**13:21** When a rich person stumbles, friends prop them up; when a poor person falls, even friends give them a shove.

**13:22** When the wealthy slip up, a crowd rushes to help; they say something wrong and people find reasons to excuse it. When the poor slip, everyone piles on with more criticism; they say something wise and nobody listens.

**13:23** When the rich speak, the room goes quiet and people praise their words to the heavens; when the poor speak, everyone asks, "Who does this person think they are?" — and if they stumble, people drive them even further down.

**13:24** There's nothing wrong with wealth — as long as no sin comes with it; but poverty is seen as something shameful in the eyes of the ungodly.

**13:25** What's in your heart shows on your face — for better or for worse.

**13:26** A radiant face is the sign of a joyful heart; finding the right words of wisdom, though — that takes real work.
